written: 2026-11-26 (UTC), before part F of scripts/research_v4e.py produced any number
status: Fixed. Hindsight; not part of the ledger; not a forecast.
why: Round 5 ended with: record industry breadth live, outside the rule. The 49-industry file it was measured on (Kenneth R. French Data Library) is published weeks late, so it cannot be recorded daily. This checks whether a breadth measure that can be collected every day carries the same information.
daily_proxy: The 11 Select Sector SPDR funds (XLB, XLC, XLE, XLF, XLI, XLK, XLP, XLRE, XLU, XLV, XLY). Source: the issuer's own NAV history files (State Street). Breadth = share of the funds with a 200-day NAV history whose NAV is below its own 200-day average; needs at least 9 funds.
known_differences: 9 to 11 sectors instead of 49 industries, so the value moves in steps of about 0.1. NAV leaves out distributions. History starts in 1999-2000, so 1990-2006 is only partly covered.
levels: The same cut points as the 49-industry measure in round 5b (its 50th, 75th and 95th percentile of 1990-2006: 0.245, 0.49, 0.857). Not refitted.

checks.same_information: Spearman rank correlation with the 49-industry breadth on common days at least 0.80
checks.near_highs: AUROC for a 10% fall within 63 days, on days within 5% of the 252-day high, 2007 on, at least 0.58
checks.in_the_rule: v3 plus the proxy as one more component (not counted toward floors): 2007-on O1 AUROC at least 0.02 above v3

reading.all three hold: The proxy is good enough to record live as a shadow indicator. Build the daily record outside the ledger chain.
reading.otherwise: Report which check failed. Record the 49-industry measure when its file is published instead, and say plainly that such a record is late.
reading.source unreachable: Report it and name what else could be tried.

what_this_is_not: Not a test of whether breadth should enter the rule. That is what the live record is for.
